_note: Run 5: Run 4 (supcon_ce_convnext_base_heldout_pairs) with one change, the SupCon loss on the disease head is replaced by a Correct-n-Contrast-style loss. Why: the diagnostics showed the SupCon disease embedding is tied to the crop (disease retrieval of unseen images 9%; 133 of 175 diseases occur on one crop only, so a disease's positives are almost always the same crop). Correct-n-Contrast (Zhang et al., ICML 2022) removes such a shortcut with cross-attribute pairs: positives are the same class with a different spurious attribute, hard negatives are a different class with the same attribute. Here: positives = same disease on a different crop (plus the image's other view); negatives = other diseases, with same-crop other diseases added by the batch sampler; same disease on the same crop is left out of both. The crop labels are known, so no ERM stage is needed to guess the attribute. Batches: of 64 images, 4 groups of 8 (2 images of one disease on each of two crops, 4 images of other diseases on the first crop; only the 42 diseases that occur on two or more crops can form groups) and 32 uniform random images, so the class mix stays near the natural one. The crop-head SupCon term, the cross-entropy heads, the held-out pairs loss, the scoring, the validation protocol and the final-fit schedule are as Run 4. Stage 1 is re-run in full because the loss changed. Epoch and gamma are chosen on validation (training data only).
_result: Run 5. Test HM Top-1 66.49 / Top-5 92.58; seen 57.00 (Top-5 86.50), unseen 79.77 (Top-5 99.59) calibrated; raw seen 71.80, raw unseen 12.22 (HM at gamma 0: 20.89 / 70.20); 28.5% of seen images sent to unseen pairs (Run 4: 21.2%). Epoch 8, gamma 8.0, validation HM 60.77 (per split 58.71 / 58.24 / 65.36; Run 4: 61.27 at epoch 17). Versus Run 4 (70.94 / 92.97): -4.5 Top-1, -0.4 Top-5; seen -6.1, unseen -1.3. Not an improvement. Seen-versus-unseen separation is unchanged (AUROC 0.923 against 0.919), the loss is in seen accuracy. The intended effect did not appear: disease 1-NN accuracy of unseen test images against the training images is 8.1% (Run 4: 9.0%, SupCon-off control: 7.5%), so the disease embedding is still tied to the crop; the pre-set success rule (9% to over 25%) failed. Validation was flat across epochs (60.77 at epoch 8, 60.46 at epoch 17), so epoch 8 was a noisy pick, and an earlier stop probably explains part of the test drop (CE-only, epoch 5: 66.39); not isolated. One seed. Decision: the SupCon-side changes are finished; SupCon stays reported as neutral.

model._note: ConvNeXt-Base from timm, ImageNet-22k pretraining then 1k fine-tuning; drop_path_rate is stochastic depth. ce_dropout matches the baseline's head dropout.

input._note: Bicubic resizing, as ConvNeXt was pretrained.

augmentation._note: Same as the independent ConvNeXt-Base baseline.

loss._note: CHANGED vs Run 4: cnc replaces the SupCon term of the disease head by the Correct-n-Contrast-style loss (dpd/supcon.py cnc_loss) and switches the batches to CnCBatchSampler: groups groups per batch, each with per_crop images of one disease on each of two crops and hard_neg images of other diseases on the first crop; the rest of the batch is random. pair_loss as in Run 4.

scoring._note: CHANGED: mode heads, the cross-entropy heads' log-probabilities. temperature is only used for the prototypes saved alongside.

optimizer._note: As the independent ConvNeXt-Base baseline (lr_head also covers the projection and cross-entropy heads).

training._note: As Run 4: final_schedule match_validation; stage 1 runs in full because the training loss changed.

runtime._note: grad_checkpointing: recompute backbone activations in the backward pass; identical gradients, less GPU memory, somewhat slower. Needed because ConvNeXt-Base with 128 views per step did not fit in 16 GB.
